strongest_case_against_the_verdict: Take the quantity as Harrell's C-index for time to MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI from a structural-MRI-plus-clinical Cox model under internal random-split validation. On the PDFs all four review gates then match: both are T2; both use ADNI; both have a random held-out split (P-13 237/103, P-1128 112/50), which is V3 by the extraction template's own definition, so P-13's registry V2 is a miscoding; and both combine structural MRI with clinical scales. The metric type is identical, and like for like the results are far apart: training 0.951 (0.928-0.974) against 0.844 (0.815-0.873), with non-overlapping intervals, and hold-out 0.880 (0.817-0.943), whose interval excludes P-13's 0.805. There is also an ordering angle: P-13 states that 'All the longitudinal models performed better than the baseline models' and that hippocampal volume is 'the best predictive marker for AD', while P-1128's baseline whole-cortex radiomics model beats P-13's longitudinal hippocampus-plus-CDRSB model, and P-1128 claims 'higher accuracy' than hippocampus-focused models. Shared ADNI participants make the comparison tighter, not looser.
why_it_does_or_does_not_succeed: It does not succeed, and the reason is the rule's definition of a contradiction, not the gate. (1) The two C-indices belong to two different models with different predictor sets and input representations. The rule lists different methods each reporting a different score, with no refuted ordering claim, as not incompatible. The interval around an apparent C-index describes the sampling variability of that fitted model on that sample, not a population parameter both papers estimate. (2) The estimand differs in population and horizon. P-13's C-index is confined to a high-risk subgroup chosen by clustering follow-up FAQ trajectories, with longitudinal inputs over visits to 96 months. P-1128 keeps only converters within 60 months and 5-year-stable patients, and excludes reverters. P-13 itself shows the size of this effect: baseline ADAS13 scores 0.677 in its high-risk group and 0.825 in its low-risk group, a spread about twice the 0.075 hold-out gap. (3) The ordering angle fails. P-13's longitudinal-over-baseline result compares versions of the same markers inside its own subgroup, and P-1128 tests no longitudinal model (it names 'did not analyze dynamic follow-up data' as a limitation). The hippocampus sentence is P-13 citing Teipel et al. 2013, not its own finding. P-1128's superiority claim is made against its refs 7 and 9, its 37 features include left-hippocampus network features, and P-13's lower figures agree with P-1128's claim rather than refute it. (4) The C-80, C-204 and C-232 precedents each had a stronger case (C-232's within-study rankings did reverse). They were reclassified as documented incommensurability on input representation, on endpoint and evaluation, and on predictor set and horizon respectively; C-262 fails on the same axes and has no ordering claim at all. (5) On the caller's question: a performance difference between two different models on overlapping ADNI data can be a genuine contradiction under the rule only in two cases. Either the same model or marker set is evaluated for the same estimand with mutually exclusive uncertainty, or one study's own head-to-head ordering is reversed by the other's on a comparable estimand. Neither holds here, and shared participants are recorded as non-independence, not as a route to contradiction. (6) The false_positive direction was also tested, since the record is a filed 'EXAMINED NON-CONFLICT' with paper_b null. Read against the documents, a gap larger than the record states survives and fails on quantity, so documented_incommensurability is the precise outcome. That matches the first reader's filed notes C-253 and C-260 and the closed precedents C-238 and C-239.
grounds: Like for like, P-1128 is higher at both evaluation levels (training 0.951, 0.928-0.974, against 0.844, 0.815-0.873; hold-out 0.880, 0.817-0.943, against 0.805), but these are C-indices of two different models, and the rule counts 'two different methods each reporting a different score where neither study claims the ordering the other refutes' as not incompatible [f2, f11].

The predictor sets and input representations differ: functional principal-component scores of longitudinal CDRSB and hippocampal volume with baseline cognition, demographics and APOE e4 in P-13, against 37 baseline cortical-morphology and gray-matter-network features with MoCA and FAQ in P-1128 [f5, f14; first reader q5].

The populations and horizons differ: P-13's estimate is confined to a high-risk subgroup chosen by clustering FAQ trajectories over visits to 96 months, whereas P-1128 keeps only converters within 60 months and patients stable for 5 years and drops reverters [f1, f4, f10, f12, f13].

P-13 itself shows how far the subgroup moves a C-index: the same baseline predictor (ADAS13) scores 0.677 in its high-risk group and 0.825 in its low-risk group (0.665 and 0.793 after optimism correction), a spread about twice the 0.075 hold-out gap between the papers [f6, f7].

No ordering claim is refuted: P-13's 'longitudinal beats baseline' is a within-subgroup result for the same markers that P-1128 never tests, P-13's hippocampus sentence cites Teipel et al. 2013 rather than its own data, and P-1128's claim of higher accuracy than hippocampus-focused models agrees with P-13's lower figures [f8, f9, f15, f16, f18].

On the PDFs the four deterministic gates can be read as matched (T2; ADNI; a random held-out split in both, V3 by the extraction template's definition, so P-13's registry V2 is a miscoding; structural MRI with clinical scales), so the gate does not block this pair; it fails the same-quantity and incompatibility tests that apply after the gates [f3, f17].

The precedents agree: C-80 (input representation), C-204 (endpoint and evaluation, no ranking contradiction) and C-232 (predictor set and horizon, although its within-study rankings did reverse) were reclassified as documented incommensurability, and C-262 is weaker than each because it contains no ordering claim.

On the caller's question: under the rule as written, a performance gap between two different models on overlapping ADNI data can be genuine only if the same model or marker set is evaluated for the same estimand with mutually exclusive uncertainty, or if one study's own head-to-head ordering is reversed by the other's on a comparable estimand; neither holds here.

It is not a false_positive although the record is a filed note with paper_b null: read against the documents, a like-for-like gap larger than the record states survives (non-overlapping training intervals) and fails on quantity, which is how the first reader treated the filed notes C-253 and C-260 and how C-238 and C-239 were closed.

corrections_to_first_reader: gates.validation_tier ('mismatch as coded, not waived'): config/extraction_template.json defines V2 as k-fold CV with no separate test set and V3 as including a held-out test partition, so P-13's random 237/103 split with a reported test-set C-index is not V2; the registry coding is wrong and the tier matches in substance for the hold-out figures without any waiver.

gates.modality_family ('mismatch in composition, not waived'): at family level both are structural MRI with clinical scales (P-13 adds APOE e4 as a covariate); the composition difference is a predictor-set difference, which the first reader's ground 3 already carries correctly, not a gate failure.

record_defects (on 'the only pair in this pack that clears all four comparability gates') and what_would_change_the_verdict overstate the gate failure: on the PDFs the review's four gates can be read as matched, so no tier or modality waiver would be needed; the verdict rests on the same-quantity test, which the first reader's five grounds already apply correctly.

No factual error in the first reader's numbers or quotes: all 16 quotes were found verbatim on the stated pages, and its like-for-like gaps (0.107 in training, 0.075 on hold-out) and its reading of Table 2 (network-morphology validation 0.844, interval midpoint 0.844, against 0.884 in the abstract and Section 3.2) check against the PDF.
